chain.label: No viable SIC advancement path / noncompliance undetected
chain.trigger: the company did not have a Learjet-qualified management pilot or check airman on staff during the accident SIC's period of employment, Trans-Pacific's graduated SIC qualification policy could not provide him... a viable, well-structured path to gain experience as a PF

chain.label: SOPs lacked manufacturer wind-additive guidance
chain.trigger: the approach speeds listed in Trans-Pacific's SOPs did not include these wind additives

chain.label: Gusting northwesterly surface wind
chain.trigger: wind from 360° at 16 kts gusting to 32 kts

chain.label: PIC's inadequate and incomplete preflight planning
chain.trigger: the flight plan listed an estimated flight time of 28 minutes and requested an en route altitude of 27,000 ft, which were not compatible with each other... no evidence that the crew obtained weather information for the accident flight leg to TEB

chain.label: PIC allowed unapproved SIC to act as pilot flying
chain.trigger: okay I think we're next man. hand on your yoke

caused_by.evidence: Trans-Pacific's graduated SIC qualification policy could not provide him and the other company Learjet SIC a viable, well-structured path to gain experience as a PF

chain.label: PIC's extensive coaching distracted him from PM duties
chain.trigger: the PIC regularly coached the SIC...from before takeoff to the final seconds of the flight. The extensive coaching likely distracted the PIC from his duties as PIC and pilot monitoring

caused_by.evidence: the PIC's extensive coaching of the SIC in his PF duties distracted the PIC, interfered with the normal division of PF and PM duties, and degraded the flight crew's overall performance

chain.label: Checklists and approach briefing omitted
chain.trigger: the flight crew began the approach but did not conduct an approach briefing

caused_by.evidence: the PIC did not...call for the Climb, Cruise, or Descent checklists (which the SIC, as PF, failed to initiate)

chain.label: Crew failed to detect improperly configured navigation equipment
chain.trigger: neither pilot detected that one of the navigation receivers was not tuned to the TEB VOR, which was necessary to identify DANDY

caused_by.evidence: This error might have been detected if an approach briefing had been conducted

chain.label: Crew mismanaged vertical profile and missed circling point
chain.trigger: crossing an intermediate fix and the final approach fix hundreds of feet above the altitudes specified by the approach procedure

caused_by.evidence: the flight crewmembers' failure to verify the approach and conduct an approach briefing resulted in confusion and errors that led them to mismanage the vertical profile

chain.label: PIC continued approach instead of executing a go-around
chain.trigger: the PIC's attempt to salvage an unstabilized visual approach

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was 2.8 nautical miles (nm) beyond the final approach fix... and could not be maneuvered to line up with the landing runway, which should have prompted the crew to execute a go-around

chain.label: PIC continued steep turn without adding power or reducing AOA
chain.trigger: the PIC continued the left turn without adding power or lowering the airplane's nose to reduce AOA

caused_by.evidence: the rapid left turn was likely the PIC's attempt to continue the approach to landing
the strong, gusting wind might have momentarily reduced the airplane's airspeed below the stall speed
including a wind additive...when calculating approach speeds would provide additional stall margin

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall during turn to final
chain.trigger: the PIC announced 'stall' in a strained voice, and the SIC replied 'yup'

caused_by.evidence: the airplane reached a left bank angle of 35°...and the airspeed decreased to about 111 kts

the left-wing-down aileron input required to make the turn to final and counter the strong (possibly gusting) left crosswind would have increased the right wing's AOA and potentially led the wing to stall first

chain.label: Airplane rolled right and departed controlled flight
chain.trigger: radar data and the security video showed that the airplane rolled to the right (away from the runway) before impact

caused_by.evidence: potentially led that wing to stall first, inducing a roll to the right

chain.label: Impact with commercial building and parking lot
chain.trigger: impacted a commercial building and parking lot

caused_by.evidence: witnesses reported seeing the airplane nearly inverted in a nose-low attitude just before impact

chain.label: Fatal injuries to both pilots
chain.trigger: The pilot-in-command (PIC) and the second-in-command died

caused_by.evidence: The airplane was destroyed by impact forces and postcrash fire
